summary: Franklin County tower near Pond Park, built 1914 and removed 1932 per the FFLOS register; no source read describes the site today.

facts.status_note: Register says the wooden tower was removed in 1932; no coordinates are listed for the site

events.note: Wooden tower built on the white rocks near Pond Park; the index says 35 feet, while a June 1914 notice planned 50 feet
Fire of fifty to sixty acres near the tower at Pond Park; nearby residents and about thirty academy students fought it
Register gives 1932 as the removal year
Registered on the Former Fire Lookout Sites register on September 16, 2008

evidence.supports: Wooden tower built in 1914 and removed in 1932
evidence.quote: This wooden tower was built in 1914 and was removed in 1932.

evidence.supports: No coordinates available for the site
Index gives a 35-foot wood tower erected in 1914
June 1914 notice: academy erecting a tower 50 feet high on the white rocks
evidence.quote: The Pennsylvania State Forest Academy at Mont Alto is erecting a tower 50 feet high on the 'white rocks.'

evidence.supports: Purpose: fire wardens could look over South Mountain and detect fires early
evidence.quote: This will enable the fire wardens to look over the entire South Mountain and detect a fire in its incipiency.

evidence.supports: Tower to be connected with the Forest Academy by telephone
evidence.quote: The tower will be connected with the Forest Academy by telephone.

evidence.supports: March 1920 fire of fifty to sixty acres near the tower at Pond Park
evidence.quote: A forest fire of large proportion swept over an area of between fifty and sixty acres near the White Rock fire tower at Pond Park in the Mont Alto forest reservation, Monday night and was only gotten under control after a hard battle by nearby residents, and the entire student personnel of the Mont Alto Forest Academy, numbering about thirty men.

evidence.supports: Academy students joined the fight against the 1920 fire
evidence.quote: the entire student personnel of the Mont Alto Forest Academy, numbering about thirty men

sources.title: White Rocks Tower Site
sources.publisher: Former Fire Lookout Sites register, Forest Fire Lookout Association

sources.title: White Rock - FOREST LOOKOUTS (quoting newspapers of 1914 and 1920)

resolved_conflicts.explanation: A June 1914 notice planned a 50-foot tower; the Weebly index says a 35-foot wood tower was erected. The 35-foot figure (10.7 m) is kept because the index states it as the built height; the planned 50 feet is noted in the story.

notes_for_editor: Removal and registration rest on the FFLOS register; build year, purpose and the 1920 fire rest on two newspaper items quoted on the Weebly index. The Weebly White Rock page also carries a 1922 item about a wildcat at 'the fire observation tower' on White Deer Mountain; it is about a different tower, so it is left out and the Weebly page may need a fix. No source read describes the site after 1932 or today, and the story says so. Reads: 4 pages (Weebly, FFLOS entry, DCNR Mont Alto history, Wikipedia Mont Alto State Park; the last two do not mention the tower); 1 search.
